covered_entities: large frontier developers (frontier developers with affiliates' annual gross revenues > USD 500 million in preceding calendar year)
covered_systems: frontier models (foundation models trained with >10^26 integer or floating-point operations)

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 服务提供者提供的生成合成服务属于《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第十七条第一款情形的，应当按照要求对文本、音频、图片、视频、虚拟场景等生成合成内容添加显式标识（如在文本、图片、视频的适当位置添加提示文字或标志，在音频中添加语音或节奏提示）；提供下载、复制、导出等功能时，应当确保文件中含有满足要求的显式标识。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Where a provider's generation/synthesis service falls under Art. 17(1) of the Deep Synthesis Provisions, it shall add explicit labels to generated text, audio, images, video, virtual scenes and other content (e.g. prompt text or symbols at appropriate positions in text, images and video; voice or rhythm prompts in audio); when offering download, copy or export functions it shall ensure the exported file contains a compliant explicit label. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.object: AI-generated text, audio, images, video, virtual scenes
clauses.requirement: perceptible AI-content labels, preserved in downloaded/exported files
clauses.condition: service falls within Deep Synthesis Provisions Art. 17(1)
clauses.purpose: inform the public that content is AI-generated
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI and deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording could not be fetched. Technical label forms specified in GB 45438-2025.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 服务提供者应当按照《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第十六条的规定，在生成合成内容的文件元数据中添加隐式标识，隐式标识包含生成合成内容属性信息、服务提供者名称或者编码、内容编号等制作要素信息；鼓励服务提供者在生成合成内容中添加数字水印等形式的隐式标识。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Pursuant to Art. 16 of the Deep Synthesis Provisions, providers shall add implicit labels in the file metadata of generated/synthesised content, containing production-element information such as the content's generated/synthetic attribute, the provider's name or code, and a content ID; providers are encouraged to add implicit labels such as digital watermarks in the content. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.requirement: machine-readable provenance metadata (attribute, provider, content ID); watermarks encouraged
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI and deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Watermarking is encouraged (SHOULD) while metadata labels are mandatory.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 提供网络信息内容传播服务的服务提供者应当核验文件元数据中是否含有隐式标识：含有的，应当在发布内容周边添加显著提示标识；未核验到隐式标识但用户声明为生成合成内容的，提示公众该内容可能为生成合成内容；均未核验到但检测到显式标识或其他生成合成痕迹的，识别为疑似生成合成内容并添加提示；并在元数据中添加传播平台名称或编码、内容编号等传播要素信息。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Providers of online content dissemination services shall check whether file metadata contains implicit labels: if so, add a prominent notice around the published content; if no implicit label is found but the user declares the content AI-generated, notify the public that it may be AI-generated; if neither but explicit labels or other generation traces are detected, identify it as suspected AI-generated content and add a notice; and add dissemination information (platform name or code, content ID) to the metadata. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.action: verify implicit labels and add prominent notices (confirmed / possible / suspected)
clauses.object: content uploaded and disseminated on the platform
clauses.requirement: tiered detection-and-labeling of AI content at distribution
clauses.condition: applies when disseminating content
clauses.applicable_systems: social media, video and other content platforms
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Three-tier confirmed/possible/suspected labeling is the distinctive feature.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 用户申请服务提供者提供没有添加显式标识的生成合成内容的，服务提供者可以在通过用户协议明确用户的标识义务和使用责任后，提供不含显式标识的生成合成内容，并依法留存提供对象信息等相关日志不少于六个月。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Where a user requests generated content without explicit labels, the provider may supply it after the user agreement makes clear the user's labeling obligations and responsibilities, and shall retain related logs (e.g. recipient information) for no less than six months. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.action: provide unlabelled content on request; retain logs
clauses.requirement: unlabelled output permitted only with user-agreement terms and >= 6 months log retention
clauses.condition: user requests unlabelled content
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI and deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Implicit (metadata) labels are not waived by this provision as the compiler understands it.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 用户使用网络信息内容传播服务发布生成合成内容的，应当主动声明并使用服务提供者提供的标识功能进行标识。任何组织和个人不得恶意删除、篡改、伪造、隐匿本办法规定的生成合成内容标识，不得为他人实施上述行为提供工具或者服务，不得通过不正当标识手段侵害他人合法权益。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Users publishing AI-generated content via dissemination services shall proactively declare it and use the platform's labeling function. No organisation or individual may maliciously delete, alter, forge or conceal AI-content labels, provide tools or services enabling others to do so, or infringe others' lawful rights through improper labeling. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.action: declare AI content; not remove/forge labels or supply removal tools
clauses.requirement: user self-declaration plus ban on label stripping, forgery and label-removal tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Combines a MUST (declare) with MUST NOT (tampering); modality set to the prohibition. Extends Deep Synthesis Art. 18.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当定期审核、评估、验证算法机制机理、模型、数据和应用结果等，不得设置诱导用户沉迷、过度消费等违反法律法规或者违背伦理道德的算法模型。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall regularly review, assess and verify algorithm mechanisms, models, data and application results, and shall not set up algorithmic models that induce user addiction or excessive consumption or otherwise violate laws and regulations or ethics. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.action: periodically audit algorithms; not deploy addictive/exploitative models
clauses.object: algorithm mechanisms, models, data and outputs
clauses.requirement: regular algorithm review/assessment; ban on addiction- or overspending-inducing models
clauses.purpose: prevent manipulative design and harm to users
clauses.applicable_systems: recommendation, ranking, filtering, scheduling and generative algorithms used in information services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Combines a positive audit duty (MUST) with a prohibition (MUST NOT) on addictive models.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当加强信息安全管理，建立健全用于识别违法和不良信息的特征库，完善入库标准、规则和程序。发现未作显著标识的算法生成合成信息的，应当作出显著标识后，方可继续传输。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall strengthen information security management and establish and improve feature databases for identifying illegal and harmful information, improving inclusion standards, rules and procedures. Where algorithmically generated or synthesised information without prominent labeling is discovered, it may continue to be transmitted only after prominent labeling has been added. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.requirement: maintain illegal-content feature libraries; label unlabelled synthetic content before continuing to distribute
clauses.condition: upon discovering unlabelled synthetic content
clauses.purpose: transparency about synthetic content, content safety
clauses.interpretation_notes: Earliest CAC rule requiring platforms to label AI-generated content; extended by CN_Deep_Synthesis_2022 and CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025 Art. 6.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当以显著方式告知用户其提供算法推荐服务的情况，并以适当方式公示算法推荐服务的基本原理、目的意图和主要运行机制等。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall inform users in a prominent manner of their provision of algorithmic recommendation services, and publicise in an appropriate manner the basic principles, purposes and main operating mechanisms of the algorithmic recommendation services. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: use of algorithmic recommendation; its basic principles, purpose and main mechanisms
clauses.requirement: algorithmic transparency notice
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'Appropriate manner' left undefined; violations sanctionable under Art. 31.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当向用户提供不针对其个人特征的选项，或者向用户提供便捷的关闭算法推荐服务的选项。用户选择关闭算法推荐服务的，算法推荐服务提供者应当立即停止提供相关服务。算法推荐服务提供者应当向用户提供选择或者删除用于算法推荐服务的针对其个人特征的用户标签的功能。算法推荐服务提供者应用算法对用户权益造成重大影响的，应当依法予以说明并承担相应责任。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall provide users with options not targeting their personal characteristics, or provide users with a convenient option to turn off algorithmic recommendation services. Where a user chooses to turn off the service, the provider shall immediately stop providing it. Providers shall provide users with functions to select or delete user tags targeting their personal characteristics used for algorithmic recommendation. Where a provider's use of algorithms has a major impact on users' rights and interests, it shall give an explanation in accordance with law and bear corresponding responsibility. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.action: provide opt-out / non-personalised option; tag management; explanation
clauses.requirement: non-personalised option or easy switch-off, immediate cessation on opt-out, user tag control, explanation where major impact
clauses.condition: explanation duty applies where algorithm has a major impact on user rights
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paragraph breaks in the source were joined. Parallels PIPL Art. 24 on automated decision-making.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者向消费者销售商品或者提供服务的，应当保护消费者公平交易的权利，不得根据消费者的偏好、交易习惯等特征，利用算法在交易价格等交易条件上实施不合理的差别待遇等违法行为。
clauses.translated_text: Where algorithmic recommendation service providers sell goods or provide services to consumers, they shall protect consumers' right to fair trade and shall not use algorithms to apply unreasonable differential treatment in transaction prices or other transaction conditions based on consumers' preferences, transaction habits or other characteristics, or commit other illegal acts. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: prices and transaction conditions based on consumer characteristics
clauses.requirement: no algorithmic price discrimination ('big-data price-killing')
clauses.condition: when selling goods or services to consumers
clauses.applicable_systems: pricing and recommendation algorithms in e-commerce/services
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'Unreasonable' differential treatment is not defined; Art. 32 refers enforcement to other laws (e.g. E-Commerce Law, pricing law).

clauses.original_text: 具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的算法推荐服务提供者应当在提供服务之日起十个工作日内通过互联网信息服务算法备案系统填报服务提供者的名称、服务形式、应用领域、算法类型、算法自评估报告、拟公示内容等信息，履行备案手续。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity shall, within ten working days from the date of providing services, complete filing procedures through the Internet Information Service Algorithm Filing System by submitting information such as the provider's name, service form, field of application, algorithm type, algorithm self-assessment report and content intended for public disclosure. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: algorithmic recommendation service provider with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.object: algorithm filing information incl. self-assessment report
clauses.requirement: algorithm registry filing within 10 working days of launch
clauses.condition: provider has public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.applicable_systems: algorithmic recommendation services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.interpretation_notes: The filing regime is reused by CN_Deep_Synthesis_2022 Art. 19 and CN_GenAI_Measures_2023 Art. 17. Changes within 10 working days; deregistration within 20 working days of termination (paras. 2-3).

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者和使用者不得利用深度合成服务制作、复制、发布、传播虚假新闻信息。转载基于深度合成服务制作发布的新闻信息的，应当依法转载互联网新闻信息稿源单位发布的新闻信息。
clauses.translated_text: Deep synthesis service providers and users shall not use deep synthesis services to produce, copy, publish or disseminate false news information. Where news information produced and published based on deep synthesis services is reposted, news information published by internet news source units shall be reposted in accordance with law. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: deep synthesis service providers and users
clauses.requirement: no use of deep synthesis for fake news
clauses.interpretation_notes: Para. 1 adds a general ban on using deep synthesis for legally prohibited information/activities.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者和技术支持者提供人脸、人声等生物识别信息编辑功能的，应当提示深度合成服务使用者依法告知被编辑的个人，并取得其单独同意。
clauses.translated_text: Where deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters provide functions for editing biometric information such as faces and voices, they shall prompt deep synthesis service users to notify the individuals being edited in accordance with law and obtain their separate consent. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters
clauses.action: prompt users to notify and obtain separate consent
clauses.object: editing of face, voice and other biometric information
clauses.recipient: service users; individuals whose biometrics are edited
clauses.requirement: prompt users to inform the depicted person and get separate consent
clauses.condition: where biometric editing functions are offered
clauses.affected_asset: biometric data, portrait and voice rights
clauses.interpretation_notes: The provider's duty is to prompt; the consent obligation itself falls on users (aligned with PIPL separate-consent rules for sensitive personal information).

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者和技术支持者提供具有以下功能的模型、模板等工具的，应当依法自行或者委托专业机构开展安全评估：（一）生成或者编辑人脸、人声等生物识别信息的；（二）生成或者编辑可能涉及国家安全、国家形象、国家利益和社会公共利益的特殊物体、场景等非生物识别信息的。
clauses.translated_text: Where deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters provide models, templates or other tools with the following functions, they shall carry out security assessments themselves or by entrusting professional bodies in accordance with law: (1) generating or editing biometric information such as faces and voices; (2) generating or editing non-biometric information such as special objects and scenes that may involve national security, the national image, national interests or the social public interest. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters
clauses.action: conduct security assessment (self or via professional body)
clauses.object: models/templates/tools generating or editing biometric or sensitive non-biometric content
clauses.requirement: security assessment for high-risk synthesis tools
clauses.condition: tool has the listed biometric or sensitive-object functions
clauses.purpose: pre-deployment risk assessment of high-risk synthesis capabilities
clauses.applicable_systems: face/voice generation and sensitive scene generation tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Para. 1 separately requires periodic review, assessment and verification of generative/synthetic algorithm mechanisms.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者对使用其服务生成或者编辑的信息内容，应当采取技术措施添加不影响用户使用的标识，并依照法律、行政法规和国家有关规定保存日志信息。
clauses.translated_text: Deep synthesis service providers shall take technical measures to add labels that do not affect user use to information content generated or edited using their services, and retain log information in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and relevant State provisions. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: all content generated or edited with the service
clauses.requirement: embed non-intrusive (implicit) identifiers in all synthetic content and retain logs
clauses.interpretation_notes: Basis for the 'implicit label' (metadata/watermark) regime later specified in CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025 Art. 5 and GB 45438-2025.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者提供以下深度合成服务，可能导致公众混淆或者误认的，应当在生成或者编辑的信息内容的合理位置、区域进行显著标识，向公众提示深度合成情况：（一）智能对话、智能写作等模拟自然人进行文本的生成或者编辑服务；（二）合成人声、仿声等语音生成或者显著改变个人身份特征的编辑服务；（三）人脸生成、人脸替换、人脸操控、姿态操控等人物图像、视频生成或者显著改变个人身份特征的编辑服务；…
clauses.translated_text: Where deep synthesis service providers provide the following deep synthesis services that may cause public confusion or misidentification, they shall place prominent labels in a reasonable position or area of the generated or edited content to alert the public to the deep synthesis: (1) text generation or editing services simulating natural persons, such as intelligent dialogue and intelligent writing; (2) speech generation such as synthetic voice and voice imitation, or editing services that significantly alter personal identity characteristics; (3) generation of images/videos of persons such as face generation, face swapping, face manipulation and posture manipulation, or editing that significantly alters personal identity characteristics; … [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: generated/edited content of listed service types (chatbots, voice cloning, face swap, immersive scenes, etc.)
clauses.requirement: prominent visible disclosure of deep synthesis
clauses.condition: service may cause public confusion or misidentification
clauses.exception: for other deep synthesis services, provider need only offer a prominent-label function and prompt users that they may label (para. 2)
clauses.applicable_systems: chatbots, writing assistants, voice synthesis, face/body synthesis, immersive realistic scenes
clauses.interpretation_notes: Items (4) immersive realistic scenes and (5) other services significantly generating/altering content were truncated. 'Explicit label' rules elaborated in CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025.

clauses.original_text: 任何组织和个人不得采用技术手段删除、篡改、隐匿本规定第十六条和第十七条规定的深度合成标识。
clauses.translated_text: No organisation or individual may use technical means to delete, alter or conceal the deep synthesis labels provided for in Articles 16 and 17 of these Provisions. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.requirement: do not remove or tamper with synthetic-content labels
clauses.interpretation_notes: Applies to everyone, not just providers.

clauses.original_text: 提供和使用生成式人工智能服务，应当遵守法律、行政法规，尊重社会公德和伦理道德，遵守以下规定：（一）坚持社会主义核心价值观，不得生成煽动颠覆国家政权、推翻社会主义制度，危害国家安全和利益、损害国家形象，煽动分裂国家、破坏国家统一和社会稳定，宣扬恐怖主义、极端主义，宣扬民族仇恨、民族歧视，暴力、淫秽色情，以及虚假有害信息等法律、行政法规禁止的内容；
clauses.translated_text: The provision and use of generative AI services shall comply with laws and administrative regulations, respect social morality and ethics, and observe the following: (1) uphold the core socialist values, and not generate content prohibited by laws and administrative regulations such as incitement to subvert state power or overthrow the socialist system, endangering national security and interests, harming the national image, inciting secession or undermining national unity and social stability, promoting terrorism or extremism, promoting ethnic hatred or discrimination, violence, obscenity and pornography, or false and harmful information; [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: providers and users of generative AI services
clauses.object: content prohibited by laws and administrative regulations
clauses.requirement: do not generate prohibited content (subversion, threats to national security, terrorism/extremism, ethnic hatred, violence, pornography, false and harmful information)
clauses.purpose: protect national security, social stability and the information environment
clauses.affected_asset: national security, social order, public information ecosystem
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI services offered to the public in the PRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Applies to both providers and users. 'False and harmful information' and political-content categories are broad and defined by reference to other laws.

clauses.original_text: （二）在算法设计、训练数据选择、模型生成和优化、提供服务等过程中，采取有效措施防止产生民族、信仰、国别、地域、性别、年龄、职业、健康等歧视；
clauses.translated_text: (2) In algorithm design, training data selection, model generation and optimisation, and service provision, take effective measures to prevent discrimination on the basis of ethnicity, belief, country, region, sex, age, occupation, health, etc.; [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: providers (and users) of generative AI services
clauses.object: discrimination by ethnicity, belief, nationality, region, sex, age, occupation, health
clauses.requirement: prevent discriminatory outputs across the lifecycle (design, data selection, training, optimisation, provision)
clauses.affected_asset: equal treatment of individuals and groups
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI services offered to the public in the PRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Lifecycle-wide 'effective measures' obligation; no technical standard named in the Measures themselves (TC260 security requirements give practice detail).

clauses.original_text: 生成式人工智能服务提供者（以下称提供者）应当依法开展预训练、优化训练等训练数据处理活动，遵守以下规定：（一）使用具有合法来源的数据和基础模型；（二）涉及知识产权的，不得侵害他人依法享有的知识产权；（三）涉及个人信息的，应当取得个人同意或者符合法律、行政法规规定的其他情形；（四）采取有效措施提高训练数据质量，增强训练数据的真实性、准确性、客观性、多样性；…
clauses.translated_text: Generative AI service providers ("providers") shall carry out pre-training, optimisation training and other training-data processing activities in accordance with law and observe the following: (1) use data and foundation models with lawful sources; (2) where intellectual property is involved, not infringe IP rights lawfully enjoyed by others; (3) where personal information is involved, obtain individual consent or meet other circumstances provided by laws and administrative regulations; (4) take effective measures to improve training-data quality and enhance its truthfulness, accuracy, objectivity and diversity; … [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: pre-training and fine-tuning data and foundation models
clauses.requirement: lawful data/model sources, no IP infringement, consent or other legal basis for personal data, effective measures for training-data quality
clauses.condition: applies to training-data processing activities
clauses.purpose: data legality, IP protection, privacy and output quality
clauses.affected_asset: intellectual property, personal information, data quality
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI models used to provide services in the PRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Item (5) (truncated) cross-refers to other requirements of the Cybersecurity, Data Security and PIPL laws and regulators.

clauses.original_text: 提供者应当按照《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》对图片、视频等生成内容进行标识。
clauses.translated_text: Providers shall label generated content such as images and videos in accordance with the Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis of Internet Information Services. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: generated images, videos and other content
clauses.requirement: label AI-generated content per the Deep Synthesis Provisions
clauses.purpose: transparency about AI-generated content, prevent public confusion
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI services offered to the public in the PRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Cross-reference to CN_Deep_Synthesis_2022 Arts. 16-18; detailed explicit/implicit label rules since 2025-09-01 in CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025 and GB 45438-2025.

clauses.original_text: 提供者发现违法内容的，应当及时采取停止生成、停止传输、消除等处置措施，采取模型优化训练等措施进行整改，并向有关主管部门报告。提供者发现使用者利用生成式人工智能服务从事违法活动的，应当依法依约采取警示、限制功能、暂停或者终止向其提供服务等处置措施，保存有关记录，并向有关主管部门报告。
clauses.translated_text: Where providers discover illegal content, they shall promptly take measures such as stopping generation, stopping transmission and deletion, take measures such as model optimisation training to rectify, and report to the relevant competent department. Where providers discover users using generative AI services to engage in illegal activities, they shall, in accordance with law and agreement, take measures such as warnings, restricting functions, or suspending or terminating service, retain relevant records, and report to the relevant competent department. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.action: stop generation/transmission, remediate model, report; sanction users
clauses.object: illegal content and illegal user activity
clauses.requirement: incident handling: takedown, model rectification, user sanctions, record retention and reporting
clauses.condition: upon discovery of illegal content or illegal user activity
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI services offered to the public in the PRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Notable for requiring model-level remediation ('model optimisation training') rather than only output filtering.

clauses.original_text: 提供具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的生成式人工智能服务的，应当按照国家有关规定开展安全评估，并按照《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》履行算法备案和变更、注销备案手续。
clauses.translated_text: Those providing generative AI services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity shall carry out security assessments in accordance with relevant State provisions and complete algorithm filing, modification and cancellation procedures in accordance with the Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendation for Internet Information Services. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.action: conduct security assessment and file algorithm
clauses.requirement: security assessment plus algorithm filing/change/deregistration
clauses.condition: service has public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.interpretation_notes: In practice this underpins CAC's generative AI service filing ('large model filing') regime; the trigger criterion is not defined in the Measures.

US DOJ moves to intervene in xAI's federal suit challenging the Act (D. Colo.)

policies.version: SB 24-205 as enacted 2024 (C.R.S. 6-1-1701 to 6-1-1707), as amended by SB 25B-004; repealed and replaced by SB 26-189
covered_entities: any person deploying a consumer-facing AI system (disclosure duty)
covered_systems: high-risk artificial intelligence systems (systems that, when deployed, make or are a substantial factor in making a consequential decision)
AI systems intended to interact with consumers
covered_activities: making consequential decisions concerning consumers in education, employment, financial/lending services, essential government services, health care, housing, insurance, or legal services
exceptions: deployers with fewer than 50 full-time employees that do not train the system with their own data (conditional exemption from risk-management, impact-assessment and public-statement duties)
systems performing narrow procedural tasks or detecting decision-making patterns without replacing human assessment
specified technologies (e.g., anti-fraud, anti-malware, cybersecurity, databases, spam filtering) unless they are a substantial factor in a consequential decision
entities subject to equivalent or stricter federal standards (e.g., certain HIPAA-covered entities, banks/credit unions, insurers subject to C.R.S. 10-3-1104.9)
conditions: Duties attach only to high-risk AI systems used in consequential decisions
Rebuttable presumption of reasonable care if developer/deployer complies with the Part and AG rules
Affirmative defense if violation discovered and cured and entity complies with a recognized risk management framework (e.g., NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001)
policies.objective: Protect Colorado consumers from algorithmic discrimination by imposing a duty of reasonable care, documentation, risk-management, impact-assessment and notice obligations on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems used in consequential decisions.
policies.conflict_rule: Enforced exclusively by the Colorado Attorney General as a deceptive trade practice; no private right of action. Entities already subject to equivalent federal requirements are carved out. Federal preemption challenges (xAI v. Weiser with DOJ intervention) pending as of compilation.

record_provenance.notes: STATUS: SB 24-205 never became operative. Its operative date moved from 2026-02-01 to 2026-06-30 (SB 25B-004, signed 2025-08-28), and before that date SB 26-189 repealed and replaced its provisions with a narrower ADMT transparency/notice framework (drops impact-assessment and risk-management program duties per secondary sources) applying from 2027-01-01. SB 26-189 signing date is 2026-05-14 per most law-firm sources (one says 2026-05-20); not verified on leg.colorado.gov, which was unreachable. The Colorado AG reportedly will not enforce until rulemaking concludes; AG proposed rules/hearing dates (reported Aug/Oct 2026) unverified. xAI v. Weiser (D. Colo.) with DOJ intervention pending; reported enforcement standstill details unverified. All clauses describe the 2024 SB 24-205 text (historical) and are paraphrased from the compiler's knowledge of the enacted bill, not fetched verbatim. Consider a separate catalogue record for SB 26-189.

clauses.original_text: A developer of a high-risk artificial intelligence system shall use reasonable care to protect consumers from any known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination arising from the intended and contracted uses of the system; compliance with the section and AG rules creates a rebuttable presumption of reasonable care.
clauses.requirement: protect consumers from known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination
clauses.condition: intended and contracted uses of a high-risk AI system
clauses.affected_asset: consumers' equal treatment in consequential decisions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Historical: repealed and replaced by SB 26-189 before becoming operative.

clauses.original_text: A developer must disclose to the Attorney General and to all known deployers or other developers any known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination arising from intended uses, without unreasonable delay and no later than 90 days after discovery (via its own testing or a credible report from a deployer).
clauses.object: known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination
clauses.requirement: report discovered discrimination risks within 90 days
clauses.condition: system has caused or is reasonably likely to have caused algorithmic discrimination
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Historical. 90-day deadline recalled from enacted text.

clauses.original_text: A deployer of a high-risk AI system shall implement a risk management policy and program governing deployment (reasonable in light of e.g. NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001) and shall complete an impact assessment of the system at least annually and within 90 days after any intentional and substantial modification.
clauses.action: implement risk management program; complete impact assessment
clauses.requirement: maintain risk management program and annual impact assessments
clauses.condition: deployment of a high-risk AI system
clauses.exception: deployers with fewer than 50 FTEs meeting statutory conditions
clauses.purpose: identify and mitigate algorithmic discrimination risks
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Historical; per secondary sources SB 26-189 drops these duties.

clauses.original_text: Before a high-risk AI system makes, or is a substantial factor in making, a consequential decision about a consumer, the deployer must notify the consumer; if the decision is adverse, the deployer must provide a statement of the principal reasons, an opportunity to correct incorrect personal data, and an opportunity to appeal that allows for human review if technically feasible.
clauses.action: notify; explain; allow correction and appeal
clauses.object: consequential decision made using a high-risk AI system
clauses.requirement: provide pre-decision notice and post-adverse-decision explanation, correction and appeal
clauses.condition: high-risk AI system is a substantial factor in a consequential decision
clauses.affected_asset: consumer's access to education, employment, credit, housing, health care, insurance, legal and government services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Historical.

clauses.original_text: A deployer or other developer that deploys or makes available an AI system intended to interact with consumers must ensure that each consumer interacting with it is told that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this would be obvious to a reasonable person.
clauses.requirement: disclose that consumer is interacting with an AI system
clauses.condition: AI system intended to interact with consumers
clauses.exception: where it would be obvious to a reasonable person
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Historical.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] Top management should demonstrate leadership and commitment by integrating AI risk management into all organizational activities, issuing a statement or policy establishing an AI risk management approach, allocating resources, and assigning authority, responsibility and accountability for managing AI risks at appropriate levels.
clauses.action: demonstrate leadership, allocate resources, assign accountability
clauses.requirement: integrate AI risk management with clear accountability and resources
clauses.purpose: embed AI risk management in governance
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase following ISO 31000 clause 5.2 with AI-specific additions; subclause heading believed correct but not verified against the official text.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should define the scope of its AI risk management activities, understand the external and internal context (including applicable legal requirements, stakeholder expectations and the AI system's intended purpose and use), and define risk criteria, including the amount and type of risk it may or may not take, taking into account impacts on individuals, groups and society.
clauses.action: define scope, context and risk criteria
clauses.requirement: set scope, context and risk criteria before assessing AI risk
clauses.purpose: tailor risk management to AI context
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, groups, society and the organization
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; mirrors ISO 31000 6.3.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should identify AI-related risks by considering assets and their value, risk sources (e.g. complexity of the environment, lack of transparency and explainability, level of automation, machine learning-specific issues, system hardware, lifecycle issues and technology readiness), potential events and outcomes, controls in place, and consequences for the organization, individuals and society.
clauses.object: AI risk sources, events, outcomes and consequences
clauses.requirement: systematically identify AI risks using AI-specific risk sources
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; the listed risk sources correspond to Annex B as summarized in secondary sources and should be verified.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should select and implement options for treating AI risks (e.g. avoiding the risk, removing the risk source, changing likelihood or consequences, sharing the risk, or retaining it by informed decision), prepare risk treatment plans, and assess whether residual risk is acceptable, taking into account AI-specific considerations.
clauses.requirement: treat AI risks and evaluate residual risk
clauses.condition: where risks exceed risk criteria
clauses.purpose: reduce AI risks to acceptable levels
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; treatment options follow ISO 31000 6.5.2.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should monitor and review the AI risk management process and its outcomes on an ongoing and periodic basis throughout the AI system life cycle, recognizing that AI systems and their context can change over time (e.g. through continuous learning or data drift).
clauses.object: AI risk management process and outcomes
clauses.requirement: continuously and periodically monitor AI risks across the lifecycle
clauses.purpose: keep risk management effective as AI systems evolve
clauses.affected_asset: AI system reliability and affected stakeholders
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; Annex C maps risk management activities to AI lifecycle stages.

clauses.purpose: set direction and accountability for responsible AI
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI systems within the AIMS scope

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define and establish an AI risk assessment process that is informed by its AI policy and objectives, produces consistent, valid and comparable results, identifies risks that could aid or prevent achieving AI objectives, analyses potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies together with their likelihood, and evaluates and prioritizes risks against risk criteria; documented information on the process shall be retained.

clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, groups, societies and the organization
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define an AI risk treatment process to select treatment options, determine the necessary controls, compare them with the controls in Annex A to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted, and produce a Statement of Applicability containing the necessary controls and justification for inclusion or exclusion; it shall formulate a risk treatment plan and obtain approval of residual risks from designated management.

clauses.requirement: treat AI risks with controls cross-checked against Annex A and document a Statement of Applicability
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.exception: Annex A controls may be excluded with documented justification
clauses.purpose: ensure appropriate controls for identified AI risks
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; mirrors ISO/IEC 27001 6.1.3 mechanics.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define a process for assessing the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, and for societies, that can result from the development, provision or use of AI systems, taking into account the technical and societal context and applicable jurisdictions; the results shall be documented and considered in the risk assessment.

clauses.requirement: perform and document AI system impact assessments feeding into risk assessment
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.purpose: protect individuals and society from adverse AI impacts
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; operationalized in Clause 8.4 and Annex A.5; detailed guidance in ISO/IEC 42005:2025.

clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope

clauses.original_text: 人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用は、不正な目的又は不適切な方法で行われた場合には、犯罪への利用、個人情報の漏えい、著作権の侵害その他の国民生活の平穏及び国民の権利利益が害される事態を助長するおそれがあることに鑑み、その適正な実施を図るため、人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の過程の透明性の確保その他の必要な施策が講じられなければならない。

clauses.original_text: 인공지능사업자는 고영향 인공지능이나 생성형 인공지능을 이용한 제품 또는 서비스를 제공하려는 경우 제품 또는 서비스가 해당 인공지능에 기반하여 운용된다는 사실을 이용자에게 사전에 고지하여야 한다.

clauses.translated_text: (2) Where an AI business operator provides generative AI or a product or service using it, it shall indicate that the output was generated by generative AI. (3) Where an AI business operator uses an AI system to provide outputs such as virtual sounds, images or videos that are difficult to distinguish from reality, it shall notify or indicate, in a manner that users can clearly recognise, that the output was generated by an AI system. …

clauses.translated_text: To ensure the safety of an AI system whose cumulative compute used for training is at or above the threshold prescribed by Presidential Decree, an AI business operator shall: 1. identify, assess and mitigate risks throughout the AI lifecycle; 2. establish a risk management system that monitors and responds to AI-related safety incidents.

clauses.recipient: Minister of Science and ICT (results must be submitted under Art. 32(2))

clauses.purpose: ensure safety of frontier AI systems
clauses.affected_asset: life, physical safety and fundamental rights
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems above the compute threshold (frontier models)

policies.objective: Establish a proportionate, context-specific and pro-innovation framework in which existing regulators apply five cross-sectoral principles to AI within their remits, supported by central government functions, rather than creating a new AI-specific regulator or horizontal AI law.

'conflicts_with' for the EU AI Act denotes a divergent regulatory philosophy (sectoral non-statutory vs horizontal statute), not a legal conflict.

policies.regulatory_regime: Utah Code Title 13 (Commerce and Trade): Chapter 72 Artificial Intelligence Policy Act and consumer protection provisions administered by the Division of Consumer Protection
policies.geo_constraints: Persons using generative AI to interact with individuals in connection with commercial activity regulated by Utah's Division of Consumer Protection, or in Utah-regulated occupations

policies.version: SB 149 (2024), as amended by SB 226 and SB 332 (2025) and HB 320 (2026)
covered_entities: persons using generative AI in commercial activity regulated by the Division of Consumer Protection
persons providing services of a regulated occupation (licensed/certified by the Utah Department of Commerce)
covered_systems: generative artificial intelligence (AI systems trained on data that interact with a person using text, audio or visual communication and generate non-scripted outputs similar to human-created outputs with limited or no human oversight)
covered_activities: provision of regulated occupational services using generative AI
participation in the AI Learning Laboratory and regulatory mitigation agreements
exceptions: SB 226 (2025) safe harbor: no violation where the generative AI itself clearly and conspicuously discloses at the outset and throughout the interaction that it is AI (per secondary sources)
conditions: After SB 226: consumer-transaction disclosure is required when the individual makes a clear and unambiguous request to know whether they are interacting with AI

After SB 226: regulated-occupation proactive disclosure required only for 'high-risk artificial intelligence interactions' (e.g., collection of sensitive personal information or provision of personalized financial, legal, medical or mental-health advice)
policies.objective: Establish disclosure obligations for generative AI use in consumer and regulated-occupation interactions, confirm that existing consumer protection law applies to generative AI, and create an Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy with a learning laboratory and regulatory mitigation agreements to foster innovation.
policies.parent_policy: Utah Consumer Protection Act / Division of Consumer Protection statutes

related_policies.policy: Utah SB 226 (2025) Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Amendments
Utah HB 320 (2026) Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy Amendments

policies.conflict_rule: Generative AI use is not a defense to violations of Utah consumer protection law; enforcement by the Division of Consumer Protection and the Attorney General under existing consumer protection statutes.

clauses.section: Utah Code 13-2-12(2) (SB 149 placement; possibly renumbered by SB 226)
clauses.original_text: It is not a defense to a violation of a statute administered and enforced by the Division of Consumer Protection that generative artificial intelligence made the violative statement, undertook the violative act, or was used in furtherance of the violation.
clauses.requirement: may not escape consumer-protection liability by attributing violations to generative AI
clauses.condition: use of generative AI in commercial activity regulated by the Division
clauses.applicable_systems: generative artificial intelligence interacting with persons
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text.

clauses.section: Utah Code 13-2-12(3) as amended by SB 226 (2025)
clauses.original_text: A person who uses generative AI to interact with an individual in connection with a consumer transaction shall disclose, clearly and conspicuously, that the individual is interacting with generative AI and not a human, if the individual makes a clear and unambiguous request or asks whether they are interacting with AI.
clauses.requirement: disclose AI use when asked
clauses.condition: consumer asks clearly and unambiguously
clauses.applicable_systems: generative artificial intelligence interacting with persons
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. SB 149 originally required disclosure if asked or prompted; SB 226 narrowed to a clear and unambiguous request.

clauses.section: Utah Code 13-2-12(4) as amended by SB 226 (2025)
clauses.original_text: A person providing the services of a regulated occupation shall prominently disclose, at the outset of the interaction, when the person is using generative AI in a high-risk artificial intelligence interaction (e.g., collecting sensitive personal information or providing personalized recommendations, advice or information that could reasonably be relied on to make significant personal decisions such as financial, legal, medical or mental-health decisions).
clauses.requirement: proactively disclose AI use at outset of high-risk interactions
clauses.condition: high-risk AI interaction in a regulated occupation
clauses.exception: safe harbor where AI itself discloses clearly at outset and throughout
clauses.affected_asset: health, financial and legal interests of individuals
clauses.applicable_systems: generative artificial intelligence interacting with persons
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Original SB 149 required proactive disclosure for all regulated-occupation interactions; SB 226 limited to high-risk interactions.

clauses.section: Utah Code Title 13, Chapter 72 (Office of AI Policy; regulatory mitigation)
clauses.original_text: The Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy administers an Artificial Intelligence Learning Laboratory Program and may enter into regulatory mitigation agreements with participants, under which participants testing AI technologies may receive reduced penalties, cure periods or other relief from applicable regulatory requirements during the agreement term.
clauses.requirement: may grant regulatory mitigation to AI learning laboratory participants
clauses.condition: participant accepted into Learning Laboratory and meets eligibility criteria
clauses.applicable_systems: AI technologies tested in the Learning Laboratory
